facts.claim: Willie Watson's 'Dancing On My Own' is a cover of Robyn's 2010 pop hit.
The song was written by Patrik Berger and Robyn, and Robyn first released it in 2010.
Robyn's original was produced by Patrik Berger and co-produced by Robyn.

The Acony Records page describes the single as Watson's answer to collective self-isolation in 2020. It says he was inspired by frequent live streaming from home and recorded the track alone in his living room.
The single was released digitally on May 15, 2020 on Acony Records. It is one 5:30 track, and the Bandcamp credit reads 'Originally performed by Robyn'.
A video of Watson performing the song was uploaded to YouTube on April 8, 2020, about five weeks before the single came out.
A 2020 Delaware Liberal write-up said it was unsurprising for Watson, an old-time specialist, to release a cover. It called his choice of Swedish disco singer Robyn the surprising part.
Watson grew up in Watkins Glen, New York, and was a founding member of Old Crow Medicine Show. He recorded and toured with the band for about 17 years before going solo in 2011.

Watson's debut solo album Folk Singer, Vol. 1 was produced by David Rawlings and released in 2014 on Acony Records, the label run by Rawlings and Gillian Welch. Folksinger, Vol. 2 followed in September 2017.
Folk Singer, Vol. 1 was recorded at Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville, which Rawlings co-owns with Welch. Unlike that album, this single was recorded alone at home.

research.lineage: Watson's work sits in the modern American folk and old-time tradition, rooted in Lead Belly, Harry Smith's anthology and string-band music. On this single he applies that stripped-down acoustic approach to a contemporary pop song.

draft:
There are no harmonies on Willie Watson's **Dancing On My Own**. Nobody joins in on a chorus, and there's no second voice to lean on. There is one fingerpicked acoustic guitar with a clear, ringing tone and heavy bass notes doing the work a kick drum used to do. Over it, Watson sings in a warm voice with a slight rasp around the edges. It's a slow, steady performance, and its plainness is the first thing that hits you.

The song belongs to Robyn. She wrote it with Patrik Berger and released it in 2010, a Swedish pop record built for dark rooms and loud systems, produced by Berger with Robyn as co-producer. That Watson would cover something wasn't news; he has spent his career inside other people's songs. As one 2020 write-up put it, the surprise was that an old-time specialist went to a Swedish disco singer for material. Watson came up as a founding member of Old Crow Medicine Show, spent about 17 years recording and touring with them, then went solo in 2011. His two Folk Singer records ran on the Lead Belly and Harry Smith anthology lineage, and he cut the first of them with David Rawlings at Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville.

This one he made alone in his living room. Acony Records framed the single as his answer to the collective self-isolation of spring 2020, sparked by all the live-streaming he'd been doing from home, and a video of him playing it surfaced in early April, about five weeks before the release. That context changes what the title means. In 2010 the phrase belonged to a club. In 2020 it described almost everyone's evening.

The recording shows where it was made. The room sounds natural and medium-sized, with no coloring added, and the guitar and voice sit apart from each other cleanly. It feels raw more than polished, like a take rather than a production. The fingerpicking keeps a gentle, rolling motion, and that's the quiet trick here. The pulse that made the original a dance song is still there, carried by a thumb on the low strings instead of a drum machine. Watson doesn't sell the song. He sings it melodically and directly, and he lets the loneliness speak through how little is going on around him.

What comes through isn't despair. It's closer to company, one person in a room making the sound of someone else's song so the people watching on the other end of a stream feel a bit less alone in theirs.

It sticks because it turns a song about being alone in a crowd into a song about being alone together, and you can hear the room he was stuck in.
